sessions.title: Units, conversions & dimensional reasoning
sessions.focus: Units as algebraic constraints on quantitative calculations.
sessions.purpose: Make nonsensical formulas visibly wrong before later work with prices, rates, volatility, time and data frequencies.
sessions.centralCapability: Carry units through calculations, perform conversion-factor chains, and reject expressions whose dimensions cannot be added or equated.
sessions.principalObstacle: Numbers are often manipulated while units are silently dropped, allowing impossible sums or conversion factors to be inverted.
requiredOwnership: Attach units to every measured quantity.
Use conversion factors equal to one so unwanted units cancel.
Check that terms being added share the same dimension.
Check that both sides of an equation have compatible dimensions.
Distinguish dimensionless percentages/ratios from quantities carrying units.
sessions.applicationScope: Length/time/count/currency examples and simple compound rates.
sessions.transferScope: A multi-step conversion or formula audit in unfamiliar units.
sessions.exitCondition: Complete one multi-step conversion and identify one dimensionally invalid formula with a precise reason.
sessions.lesson: Treat units like symbolic factors. For 72 km/h, multiply by1000 m/km and1 h/3600 s; km andh cancel. Addition requires like units. Ratios such as 5% are dimensionless unless defined otherwise.

sessions.title: Estimation, scale & numerical sanity checks
sessions.focus: Order-of-magnitude estimates, bounds and separating exact calculation from plausibility checking.
sessions.purpose: Train the habit of catching impossible outputs before trusting a spreadsheet, model or code path.
sessions.centralCapability: Produce a defensible rough estimate, compare it with an exact result, and use magnitude/bounds to flag implausible answers.
sessions.principalObstacle: Exact arithmetic can produce false confidence when an input, unit or decimal place was entered incorrectly.
requiredOwnership: Round quantities deliberately for a rough estimate.
Track powers of ten separately from leading digits.
State whether an estimate is upper/lower/central when relevant.
Compare exact and estimated answers by relative scale.
Reject results that violate obvious bounds or sign constraints.
sessions.applicationScope: Finite products, percentages, counts and Fermi-style one-step estimates.
sessions.transferScope: A changed-scale problem where a misplaced decimal would produce a tenfold or hundredfold error.
sessions.exitCondition: Before exact computation, produce a reasonable range or order of magnitude and use it to assess the exact result.
sessions.lesson: Estimate first by replacing awkward numbers with nearby friendly ones. Keep powers of ten explicit. The estimate need not be exact; it must be good enough to catch sign errors, unit errors or misplaced decimals.

sessions.title: Powers, roots & scientific notation
sessions.focus: Exponent laws, principal square roots and scientific notation.
sessions.purpose: Create a stable symbolic/numerical base for logarithms, growth, variance scales and later algebra.
sessions.centralCapability: Evaluate and simplify integer/rational powers in elementary cases, handle principal roots correctly and combine scientific notation without losing scale.
sessions.principalObstacle: Exponent laws are often applied across addition, and √(a²) is incorrectly replaced by a without considering sign.
requiredOwnership: Use product/quotient/power exponent laws on multiplicative expressions.
Interpret negative exponents as reciprocals for nonzero bases.
Use principal square root as the nonnegative root.
Write and operate on normalized scientific notation.
Check powers-of-ten scale separately from mantissas.
sessions.applicationScope: Real numerical expressions with integer exponents, simple rational powers and principal roots.
sessions.transferScope: A mixed scientific-notation expression or sign-sensitive root identity.
outOfScope: General logarithm laws reserved for M02
sessions.exitCondition: Correctly simplify one mixed exponent/scientific-notation expression and state the sign condition behind √(a²)=|a|.
sessions.lesson: Exponent rules apply to products, not sums: a^m a^n=a^(m+n), (a^m)^n=a^(mn), and a^(−n)=1/a^n for a≠0. The principal square root is nonnegative, so √(a²)=|a|. Scientific notation keeps one nonzero digit before the decimal point.

sessions.title: Algebraic expressions, substitution & expansion
sessions.focus: Variables as placeholders, exact substitution, distributivity and collection of like terms.
sessions.purpose: Move from arithmetic to symbolic manipulation without treating symbols as labels that can be changed inconsistently.
sessions.centralCapability: Evaluate an algebraic expression at specified values, expand products and collect like terms while preserving equality.
sessions.principalObstacle: Partial substitution and sign mistakes during distribution are common, especially when negative values enter powers or products.
requiredOwnership: Substitute the full given value for each variable with parentheses when needed.
Apply distributivity to every term in a bracket.
Collect only genuinely like terms.
Preserve equality at each simplification step.
Verify a symbolic simplification by testing one legal numerical input.
sessions.applicationScope: Polynomial expressions in one or two variables.
sessions.transferScope: A fresh expression with negative substitutions or nested distributive structure.
sessions.exitCondition: Expand/simplify one unfamiliar polynomial expression and verify it at a chosen input.
sessions.lesson: For substitution, replace the symbol by the entire supplied value, using parentheses around negatives. Distributivity means a(b+c)=ab+ac. Terms combine only when they have the same variable powers.

sessions.title: Factoring & algebraic identities
sessions.focus: Factoring as reverse distributivity and use of a small set of transparent identities.
sessions.purpose: Prepare equation solving and later symbolic simplification without relying on pattern-matching alone.
sessions.centralCapability: Factor elementary polynomial expressions by common factors, grouping or standard quadratic identities and verify by re-expansion.
sessions.principalObstacle: A guessed factorization may look plausible but fail because middle terms or signs are not checked.
requiredOwnership: Extract the greatest common factor first.
Recognize difference of squares as (a−b)(a+b).
Factor simple monic and non-monic quadratics by matching product and sum.
Verify every factorization by expansion.
Distinguish factoring a sum from illegally cancelling terms.
sessions.applicationScope: Elementary polynomial expressions up to quadratic/cubic forms built from simple identities.
sessions.transferScope: A non-monic quadratic or disguised difference-of-squares example.
sessions.exitCondition: Factor one unfamiliar non-monic quadratic and verify the factorization by expansion.
sessions.lesson: Factoring reverses expansion. For ax²+bx+c, seek factors whose cross terms sum to bx. Verification is cheap: multiply the factors back out. Never 'cancel' pieces across addition.
